speaker: Host
text: Welcome, thanks for coming on the show. Today we are talking about breathing.

speaker: Guest
text: Thanks for having me, I have been looking forward to this.

speaker: Host
text: Why breathing, and why now? We did a session together last week.

speaker: Guest
text: Right, you experienced it yourself, so this is a good moment to talk about it.

speaker: Host
text: Tell people briefly who you are.

speaker: Guest
text: I am a 500-hour teacher, I work with pranayama and with the vagus nerve.

speaker: Host
text: Let's start with physiology. What happens when I lengthen the exhale?

speaker: Guest
text: A longer exhale activates the parasympathetic system. You see it on HRV immediately.

speaker: Guest
text: It is measurable, it is not esoteric. A pulse oximeter is enough to see it.

speaker: Host
text: What about CO2 tolerance? I keep hearing about Buteyko.

speaker: Guest
text: Breath holds after the exhale. It raises carbon dioxide tolerance, and it helps with anxiety.

speaker: Host
text: I try to breathe through my nose when I train. Does that make sense?

speaker: Guest
text: It does. Nitric oxide is produced in the nasal cavities and it improves perfusion.

speaker: Host
text: Some of my listeners have done ayahuasca. How does breathwork compare?

speaker: Guest
text: Breath is an altered state without chemistry. Similar quality, very different accessibility.

speaker: Guest
text: A seven-hour trip is not practical in ordinary therapy. Twenty minutes of breathing is.

speaker: Host
text: So they are complementary rather than competing.

speaker: Guest
text: Exactly. I have clients who combine both and it works well when it is integrated.

speaker: Host
text: Any book you recommend?

speaker: Guest
text: James Nestor wrote Breath, that is a good introduction. We will put the link in the description.

speaker: Host
text: We will. And do you see this as building something parallel?

speaker: Guest
text: Yes, small groups where it resonates. I am not trying to reach everyone.

speaker: Host
text: That is a good place to stop. Thank you.

speaker: Guest
text: Thank you, it was a pleasure.

speaker: Host
text: See you next episode.
